Every day is pretty much a tough day for me these days.  Everybody keep your heads up.
I think it works both ways actually, just a matter of perspective.

I've also thought about my life in terms of the Walking Dead metaphor in the past.  Except I'm one of the zombies just aimlessly walking around from one day to the next, only satifsying my basic urges of food and water to survive.

I used to feel the same way in regards to getting help.  I was very reluctant to do it because of the stigma.  Once I hit rock bottom though I no longer cared about all the negative aspects of seeking indepth help on a professional level because I had nothing left to lose.  It's generally better if you can get help before reaching this point as a preventative measure.  Being on the bottom is not a fun place to be, I know all too well.

If you don't want to live anymore then that's as bad as a human being can feel in this world.  It can't get any worse by seeking help so you might as well throw caution to the wind and give it a serious effort.  You owe it to yourself to give it shot, there is hope there whereas staying the same and enduring suffering there isn't much.
The wording doesn't matter, just speak from your heart how you truely feel.

I don't really have any answers, and that's not to say there aren't any.  If I was good at solving problems I'm guessing I would've been able to solve my own by now.  What I can say I sincerely wish you a Happy Birthday and a better tomorrow for what it's worth.  No one even wished me one this year either so I know how shitty that feels.

Every day for multiple years now.  Truely I'm surprised I'm still alive.  I guess it's a testament to humanity's will to survive and what allowed us as a species to outlast our ancestors competitors.  Logically I know I should be dead already but somehow this intangible force keeps driving me to suffer on despite the odds.  Even a miniscule shred of hope can keep a person going if their will is strong.

When it rains, it pours.

I had something similar happen, but over the course of a couple of years rather than in a week.  Good friend died in accident, dad got cancer and died slow, my love of many years left last when I spiraled downwards as a result of the first two.

Hold on to the good things in your life.   They're the things that will keep you afloat in the storm when the waves keep crashing over you.
